Source: http://www.marijuananews.com

Posted April 10, 2000

I am very pleased to announce the return of MarijuanaNews and the launching of the 4:20 MarijuanaNews radio on www.Pot-TV.net.

Starting today Monday, April 10, 2000, MarijuanaNews will resume publication of news analysis, and a complete news update will be available weekdays in Internet audio on Pot-TV.net " live " streaming at 4:20 PM and again at 7PM Pacific time, and it will soon be available " on demand " by clicking on the appropriate icon.

As regular readers of MarijuanaNews know, this is something that I have been wanting to do for some time.

In the two and half years that I have been doing MarijuanaNews, the volume of news to report has grown to be more than I could handle. This has been frustrating for me and also for some activists who could not understand why I wasn’t reporting on their activities.

At the same time, the sources of text news have also multiplied. In addition to Mapinc.org, the mother of all news sources, there are also a number of other sites concentrating on marijuana news items, notably PlanetMarijuana.com, the new effort from the indefatigable TenFreak and Marijuana.com

During all of the time that I have been involved in the marijuana resistance movement, I have generally tried to avoid duplicating the efforts of others and have tried to concentrate on whatever unique contribution that I thought that could bring to the effort.

Internet radio is a way to reach even more people with even more news and analysis.

However, there are some topics that require the sort of in depth analysis that is best provided in writing – with links to the archives of MarijuanaNews. Consequently, I will continue to offer one or two analytical pieces weekdays on MarijuanaNews.com.

All of this is made possible by the support of Marc Emery, the Canadian seed entrepreneur and the publisher of Cannabis Culture Magazine and the producer of Pot-TV.net. Marc has long been one of the most generous supporters of the efforts to end marijuana prohibition.

Many thanks to Marc.

And many thanks to all of you who sent me such kind wishes when I suspended MarijuanaNews. I was greatly cheered by your comments, and spurred to get back into the fray.

Richard Cowan
